Are there any games that defy the "Rushed game is bad forever." saying?
VtM: Bloodlines after you apply the unofficial patch (does it still count if it technically requires a mod?)
I'd say Arcanum counts too. It was buggy as fuck until it got patched.

I just bought that game during the Steam Summer Sale and played through it (with the unofficial patch) this last week. It was well done, but I'm not sure if I'll ever bother re-playing it like I have with the KotOR games.
Believe it or not, Planescape Torment was rushed at the end and that's why the game content was a bit sparse in the second half of the game.

Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords. Even without the Restored Content mod it's a decent game, considering all they had to strip out at the end to make their release deadline. Yeah, the base game is buggy as hell at times and parts of it don't make any sense (because of the content they removed), but the core was solid and interesting.

With the Restored Content mod it's even better - not only does the game have another couple of hours of content added back in, but they fixed a lot of the bugs that would cause the game to crash.
Super Smash a row Melee was in development for less than 15 months, and we know how well regarded it is.
Pretty much none of the reasons it's well regarded are intended things though. Modern techniques in Melee are just exploiting all of the stuff they decided were "known shippable" bugs/exploits.

KOTR2, for the most part. There was a bunch of cut content (there's a fan patch to restore it) and the ending was pretty bad; otherwise it's decent.

Wind Waker was decent considering the Triforce hunt and two missing dungeons.

I don't know if it counts but Gang Garrison 2 was made for a gamejam but it got a lot of development afterwards.

Mario Kart 7 isn't a terrible game, and that was so rushed they had to get Retro Studios in to help out. It's not the best Mario Kart game, sure, but it's still generally a good one overall.

The Legend of Zelda Majora's Mask was made in a year. That's seen as one of the best games ever made.

Donkey Kong Country got one game a year, at least in the SNES days. The first two are considered some of the best platformers on the system, and the third one is considered a good game overall.

I think Diddy Kong Racing was made in about a year too, and was even released to give people something to buy while waiting for Banjo-Kazooie. Doesn't stop it being a fantastic racing game, and giving Mario Kart some solid competition in the Nintendo 64 era.
Gonna say Titanfall and the so called "Star Wars: Battlefront". It's not that they're bad but get boring after a while and lack any other content besides online multiplayer. .
